2610.13039.COMMENT: Star-formation-driven outflows and CGM in starburst dwarf NGC 4214
2610.13039.title: Redshifted Cool Gas in the Disturbed HI Disk of the Starburst Dwarf NGC 4214
2610.13039.abstract: We report redshifted cool gas toward the central star-forming region of the nearby starburst dwarf galaxy NGC 4214. HST/COS spectra show low-ionization absorbers redshifted relative to the systemic velocity, most clearly in SII ($Δv=19.8\pm2.6\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$) and supported by MgII ($Δv=30.3\pm3.0\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$), while PII remains tentative ($Δv=7.5\pm3.4\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). The Keck/HIRES spectra also reveal a redshifted CaII absorption component ($Δv=25.6\pm1.5\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). Because the absorption is detected against the central UV or optical continuum, the gas must lie in the foreground of the star-forming region and is moving away from the observer and toward the background UV source in projection. A VLA--THINGS HI spectrum extracted at the COS position within one VLA beam also shows a redshifted neutral component at $v_{\rm hel}=329.2\pm0.9\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$, offset by $38.2\pm1.3\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from systemic and by $27.6\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from the dominant local HI component. The FAST HI mapping further reveals an extended, kinematically disturbed neutral disk, with residual structures relative to a warped-disk model. Together, the redshifted UV absorption, the redshifted HI component, and the disturbed large-scale HI velocity field show that the central anomalous cool gas is observed in a galaxy with a disturbed extended neutral disk. This geometry suggests that the redshifted cool gas may trace inflow or recycled fallback toward the central region, although warped-disk or non-circular disk motions cannot be fully excluded.

2610.11404.COMMENT: New stellar models and oxygen isotopic clock for RGB stars
2610.11404.title: Oxygen isotopic ratio in open cluster RGB stars: A new method for accurate mass and age estimations
2610.11404.abstract: Determining precise and homogeneous absolute ages of open clusters (OCs) remains a challenge in stellar astrophysics, mainly due to parameter degeneracies in photometric methods and line-of-sight extinctions. We present a novel method for estimating the ages of intermediate-age and old OCs, based on the strong initial-mass dependence of the surface oxygen isotopic ratio, 16O/17O, measured in RGB stars following the first dredge-up. Using updated theoretical stellar models computed with the FuNS code, we demonstrate how post-FDU CNO isotopic abundances reflect initial stellar masses. We analysed high-resolution near-infrared spectra for 11 RGB stars belonging to four Galactic OCs. For the intermediate-age clusters NGC 7789, NGC 7044, and NGC 6819, we derive ages of 1.80, 1.81, and 2.31 Ga, respectively. For the two stars in NGC 6819 the derived initial stellar mass (1.625 Mo) and age are in excellent agreement with independent estimates from asteroseismology and eclipsing binaries. Conversely, ages estimated by means of machine learning algorithms, trained to recognise specific features in the cluster CMDs, are systematically lower. Regarding the old and super-metal-rich cluster NGC 6791, the low signal-to-noise ratio and the possible line blending hinder precise mass and age constraints. With these limitations, we can only fix a lower bound of about 4 Ga for its age. The surface oxygen isotopic ratio in RGB stars provides a powerful, independent stellar clock, making high-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy of oxygen isotopes a key tool for Galactic archaeology.

2610.14169.COMMENT: Milky Way globular clusters, merger history, accreted assembly
2610.14169.title: Cluster Ages to Reconstruct the Milky Way Assembly (CARMA). VI. The age-metallicity relation of in-situ clusters and the age of the Universe
2610.14169.abstract: Within the homogeneous framework for the derivation of GC ages defined by the CARMA collaboration, we focus on the clusters born in-situ in the MW. As they are the oldest among the old GCs, their absolute age provides constraints about the age of the Universe. Moreover, the shape of their AMR is expected to show the imprints of past merger events, in case these were able to trigger GC formation in the Galaxy. We derive new homogeneous ages for 18 GCs dynamically and/or chemically classified as in-situ, and build the MW AMR from a total sample of 34 GCs. We find that all the selected GCs follow a well defined AMR, with the exception of NGC6642 and Pal1. While the former is likely a member of the LKH merger event, thus putting chronological evidence for the existence of this progenitor on even more robust ground, for the latter we propose an alternative scenario according to which it formed in-situ, but in a metal-depleted region of the Galaxy, possibly due to the interaction with an unspecified merger event. To find evidence of merger-driven GC formation, we use a GMM for the observed age distribution. This is statistically best-fit by 4 components, which we associate with significant events of the MW merger history. Cluster ages were finally calibrated to a more accurate absolute age scale based on asteroseismic measurements of the mass of red giant stars in NGC6791, and the resulting AMR was fit to compute the look-back time for the beginning of cluster formation in the MW. The fit yields t_GC,i=13.59+0.33-0.32 Gyr for initial cluster formation, and tU=13.79+/-0.34 Gyr for the age of the Universe. This value translates to H0=68.72+3.95-3.49(stat.)+2.65-2.32(sys.) km s-1 Mpc-1, where the systematic error comes from a realistic estimate of the zero point uncertainty on the GC absolute ages derived from stellar models.

2610.12159.COMMENT: Numerical galaxy simulations (FIRE) with new post-processing physics
2610.12159.title: Modeling CO Line Luminosity Using FIRE Simulations: I. Methodology and Validation of Molecular Gas and CO Abundance
2610.12159.abstract: We present a post-processing pipeline that predicts CO line luminosities, molecular hydrogen masses, and CO abundances for galaxies in the Feedback in Realistic Environments (FIRE-2) simulations, as a first step toward CO response functions for line intensity mapping mocks. SKIRT gives the radiation field reaching each gas cell. CLOUDY, tabulated on a five-parameter grid (metallicity, density, turbulent velocity, radiation field, cloud scale) and interpolated, gives $L'_{\rm CO(1-0)}$ and the $\rm H_2$ and CO masses. In this first of three papers we validate the pipeline against observations. For Milky Way (MW) molecular clouds, the predicted $L'_{\rm CO(1-0)}$ rises sharply at $A_V\sim1$ and matches the observed values above that column. For a uniform $3\,Z_\odot$ the summed luminosity is within 35\% of the observed total. A factor of three increase in metallicity changes the total $L'_{\rm CO(1-0)}$ by an order of magnitude. Along MW sight lines, the predicted $N_{\rm CO}/N_{\rm H_2}$ reproduces the observed upturn within 0.3 dex in $N_{\rm H_2}$ but falls below the data at higher columns. At $z=0$ our molecular gas masses agree with xCOLD GASS for ${\rm SFR}\gtrsim0.3\,M_\odot\,yr^{-1}$ and are converged across our simulation resolutions. At $z\gtrsim1$ observed gas masses exceed ours at fixed stellar mass, though selection effects and conversion-factor assumptions limit this comparison. CO luminosities are compared with extragalactic observations in Paper II. Capturing the metallicity-dependent dust shielding of CO from photodissociation is essential for modeling CO emission in low-mass and high-redshift galaxies.

2610.12729.COMMENT: High-resolution galaxy simulation with new synthetic FIR star formation analysis
2610.12729.title: Bridging Theory and Observation: Synthetic Far-infrared Insights into Star Formation Efficiency
2610.12729.abstract: The star formation efficiency per free-fall time ($ε_{\rm ff}$) quantifies how efficiently giant molecular clouds (GMCs) convert gas into stars and is often observed to be orders of magnitude lower than expected for free-fall collapse. Observers typically estimate $ε_{\rm ff}$ by mapping far-infrared (FIR) dust emission to infer gas surface densities ($Σ_{\rm gas}$) and counting embedded protostars, assuming simplified lifetimes and masses. Using the fiducial STARFORGE radiation-magnetohydrodynamics simulation of an $M_{\rm cl} = 2\times10^4 M_\odot$ GMC that self-consistently models star cluster formation and stellar feedback, we generate synthetic FIR observations and apply the same methodologies used in GMC surveys to investigate this discrepancy. We present the first $ε_{\rm ff}-Σ_{\rm gas}$ analysis in a fully feedback-regulated GMC simulation that resolves the formation of stellar systems. Our synthetic measurements reproduce the low observationally inferred efficiencies, showing that feedback-regulated star formation naturally produces $ε_{\rm ff} \sim 1-3\%$ without requiring extreme initial conditions. We also find that $ε_{\rm ff}$ varies strongly over a GMC's lifetime, suggesting that much of the observed scatter reflects evolutionary sampling rather than intrinsic cloud-to-cloud differences. Finally, by comparing observational and simulation definitions, we show that methodological assumptions introduce systematic biases, with a transition near $\log Σ_{\rm gas} \approx 2.3 M_\odot {\rm pc}^{-2}$ that depends on resolution. Above this threshold, the smoothing of dense structure increases both the inferred free-fall time and enclosed gas, with the latter dominating and suppressing $ε_{\rm ff}$. Below the threshold, the discrepancies are primarily driven by star formation rate assumptions.

2610.12450.COMMENT: Magellanic Cloud satellite pulsar population, near-field cosmology
2610.12450.title: Discovery of Hidden Extragalactic Pulsars in the Parkes Archival Data
2610.12450.abstract: Just over 1% of the known radio pulsar population resides in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (MCs), the satellite galaxies that are 50-62 kpc distant from the Milky Way. These pulsars are important for constraining the peak of the pulsar luminosity function, and may give insights into neutron star populations formed from stars of different metallicities than the Milky Way. Using search techniques that have proven highly effective at discovering a large number of pulsars in archival data by folding candidates near the noise floor at high harmonic folds, we reprocessed the original Parkes Multibeam MC surveys and discovered six pulsars. Five of these pulsars are located in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), including one with a spin period of 3.8s, making it the slowest pulsar known in the MCs. The remaining pulsar was detected toward the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), and is associated with the Milky Way foreground. Four of the newly discovered pulsars exhibit scintillation, with one showing clear nulling and others showing possible nulling behavior. These discoveries bring the total number of radio pulsars known in the LMC to 49. A luminosity function and duty cycle analysis of all current MC pulsars shows that they are consistent with Galactic canonical pulsars. Population synthesis simulations suggest that deeper surveys would reveal many more pulsars in the MCs, including up to handful of millisecond pulsars, based on the adopted upper limits for their parent populations. Finally, this reprocessing demonstrates the continued importance of reanalyzing archival data, both to improve the completeness of pulsar surveys and detect scientifically valuable objects.

2610.12394.COMMENT: Semi-analytic galaxy model with mass-loading factor and outflows
2610.12394.title: Inflow-driven galaxy evolution - II: A hierarchy in the scaling relations of star-forming galaxies
2610.12394.abstract: The star-forming main sequence (SFMS; $M_\star$--sSFR), the gas-to-stellar mass relation ($M_\star$--$M_{\rm gas}/M_\star$), and the mass--metallicity relation (MZR; $M_\star$--$Z_{\rm gas}$) are three core scaling relations for star-forming galaxies, and together they encode the information about the baryon cycle that operates during galaxy evolution. We investigate how these relations emerge by modelling the gas flows that regulate the baryon cycle, using both an ideal and a cosmological gas flow model, and identify a hierarchy among the three relations, with one further parameter entering the scatter budget at each step. In our model, the SFMS and its scatter are set primarily by the formation time of the host halo, with a weak dependence on the star formation efficiency and the mass-loading factor. The gas-to-stellar mass relation follows from the ratio of the sSFR to the star formation efficiency, and inherits the scatter of both. The MZR in turn follows from the gas-to-stellar mass relation together with the mass-loading factor, their relative contributions depending on the galaxy evolutionary state between the inflow-driven regime and equilibrium. This hierarchy naturally introduces further correlations among the three relations, such as the fundamental plane of star formation ($M_\star$--$M_{\rm gas}$--SFR), the fundamental metallicity relation ($M_\star$--SFR--$Z_{\rm gas}$) and its gaseous counterpart ($M_\star$--$M_{\rm gas}$--$Z_{\rm gas}$), and the correlations of each relation with galaxy size, which traces the star formation efficiency through the star formation law. Together, the three core scaling relations and the higher-dimensional correlations among them follow from a single framework, providing a foundation for linking the observables of star-forming galaxies to the underlying baryon cycle.

2610.11588.title: Measuring radial flows in disc galaxies
2610.11588.abstract: Numerous theoretical studies suggest that gas accretion from the intergalactic medium is essential to feed star formation in galaxies throughout cosmic time. However, the mechanism of gas accretion remains poorly understood, as direct evidence is lacking. In some models, gas accretion is expected to take place in the outer discs of galaxies, from where it should be transferred to the inner star-forming discs through radial flows. Finding such flows and quantifying them, therefore, opens the possibility of inferring the detailed properties of the accreting gas. Unfortunately, detecting radial flows is challenging due to the large disparity between radial and rotational velocities. Additionally, the distortions in velocity fields produced by these flows resemble the effects of warped structures, further complicating their quantification. To address this, we have developed a new methodology to measure axisymmetric radial velocities in disc galaxies. Relying on the 3D kinematic fitting software \texttt{$^{\rm 3D}$Barolo}, we have designed a dedicated workflow to measure axisymmetric radial motions in disc galaxies and to obtain robust uncertainty estimates through a bootstrapping approach. We validated this approach using realistic axisymmetric mock galaxies as well as a small sample of `observed' Milky Way-like galaxies drawn from the TNG50 hydrodynamic simulation. These tests demonstrate that our method works well and is capable of overcoming the degeneracy between radial motions and warps. The TNG50 galaxies we analysed have large regions in their discs with non-axisymmetric inflows and outflows, but they show, on average, no global trend of coherent radial flows.

2610.11763.title: Metallicity does not reorder line-to-line sensitivity to granulation in solar-like stars
2610.11763.abstract: Stellar granulation imprints line-dependent wavelength shifts and profile variations that limit the precision of radial velocity (RV) measurements used for exoplanet detection and characterization. Understanding how the sensitivity of individual spectral lines to granulation depends on stellar parameters is therefore essential for mitigating granulation-induced RV signals. Here, we investigate the effect of metallicity using MURaM 3D magnetohydrodynamic simulations of stellar granulation including a small-scale dynamo for metallicities $\mathrm{M/H}=\{-1.0,-0.5,0.0,0.3,0.5\}$. We synthesize spectra of neutral and ionized lines spanning a broad range of lower excitation potentials and transition probabilities using the MPS-ATLAS code, assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium. We quantify the sensitivity to granulation using the continuum-intensity-weighted standard deviations of the line centre-of-gravity wavelength and equivalent width, denoted by $σ_λ$ and $σ_W$, respectively. Both metrics increase systematically with metallicity at disc centre owing to the combined effects of more vigorous convection and metallicity-dependent changes in the line opacity. We find that the correlation between the solar ($\mathrm{M/H}=0.0$) and non-solar sensitivity metrics remains high from the disk center to the stellar limb. This indicates that the relative ordering of line sensitivities is robust against changes in viewing angle and metallicity. Consequently, line masks calibrated on the solar spectrum can be reliably applied to radial-velocity measurements of stars with non-solar metallicities, provided they have solar effective temperature and surface gravity.

2610.12591.title: When dust growth takes over: the origin of dust in post-reionization galaxies
2610.12591.abstract: The post-reionization epoch ($z\sim4$-6) marks a critical phase in galaxy evolution, during which galaxies rapidly assemble their stellar mass, enrich their interstellar medium, and build up substantial dust reservoirs. The physical processes responsible for such rapid dust enrichment remain uncertain. We investigate the dust enrichment history of the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST (ACJ) sample using the semi-analytic galaxy formation model GAlaxy Evolution and Assembly (GAEA), which follows galaxy assembly, chemical enrichment, and dust evolution. We select model galaxies matching the observed stellar masses, star formation rates, and metallicities of the ACJ sample, compare their dust properties with observed scaling relations, and trace their enrichment histories and environments. The model reproduces the observed dust mass-stellar mass relation and the dust-to-stellar mass, dust-to-gas, and dust-to-metal ratios as functions of stellar mass and metallicity. Reproducing these constraints requires efficient dust growth in the interstellar medium; stellar dust production alone cannot account for the observed dust reservoirs, even under the most optimistic assumptions. The combination of stellar mass, star formation rate, and metallicity provides a good predictor of galaxy dust content. Our model suggests rapid dust build-up consistent with the previously noted rapid metal enrichment, with evidence for a transition around $z\sim8$-9 below which dust growth becomes the dominant dust formation channel. Finally, ACJ-like galaxies preferentially reside in locally overdense environments, suggesting that environment may have contributed to their accelerated evolution. Taken together, these results support rapid and coupled stellar, metal, and dust build-up in ACJ galaxies during the post-reionization era.

2610.13920.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
2610.13920.abstract: Emission-line galaxies provide key diagnostics of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across cosmic time. We present a systematic census of emission-line sources using JWST/NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy (WFSS) from the COSMOS-3D program, which covers a large contiguous area of 0.33 deg$^2$ and provides F444W grism spectroscopy over $3.9$--$5.1\ μ$m. By combining slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging data, we construct a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of 12,275 objects at redshift 0--9. The typical $3σ$ line-flux limit reaches $3.2\times10^{-18}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}\ cm^{-2}}$. To address source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy, we develop a multi-step identification framework that combines information from spectra, images, spectral energy distributions, and spatial distributions. We introduce convolutional neural network and large language model to emulate the human identification process and improve efficiency. The resulting catalog provides spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties for all sources. The F444W WFSS enables the detection of multiple emission lines, including primarily [O III], H$α$, He I $\lambda10830$, [S III] $λ\lambda9531,9069$, Pa$β$, Pa$α$, Br$β$, PAH, Br$α$, allowing a continuous census of galaxies across cosmic time. We construct composite spectra in several redshift bins and detect a variety of faint spectral features that are difficult to identify in individual spectra, including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and [Fe II] lines. This catalog provides a key reference dataset for studies of galaxy evolution and AGN activity, and demonstrates the power of WFSS for constructing large, unbiased spectroscopic samples over wide areas. The full catalog will be publicly available online upon publication.

2610.12259.title: An analytical model for non-local stochastic field-level galaxy bias on the sphere
2610.12259.abstract: We present the `Bias of Overdensities in Large-scale Tracers on the Sphere' (BOLTS) model, a novel analytic galaxy bias model for projected fields on the sphere that incorporates stochasticity and non-locality already at linear order while enforcing physicality and statistical isotropy. Rather than as a deterministic transfer function, we model galaxy bias as a statistically isotropic random field, allowing stochasticity to enter through fluctuations in the bias itself. The construction yields an explicit decomposition into a linear, non-local stochastic and deterministic components in harmonic space. We fit the model parameters to the projected power spectra measured in large-volume hydrodynamical simulations (FLAMINGO), enabling sampling of galaxy populations from simulated matter fields while conditioning on galaxy properties such as halo mass or redshift. By construction, the model reproduces the two-point statistics down to the simulation resolution, and without being calibrated on it, BOLTS recovers the equilateral bispectrum within the sample variance of the simulation down to comoving scales of $\mathcal{O}(10 \, \mathrm{Mpc})$ for halo masses $ M_{\rm{h}} > 10^{11.5}\,\rm{M}_{\odot} $ over redshifts $0 < z < 3$. Relative to local bias prescriptions, it more accurately captures amplitude-phase correlations and mode coupling in the measured wavelet phase harmonics wherever the stochasticity of the tracers exceeds their discreteness, including low redshifts and lower halo masses $M_{\rm{h}} = 10^{11.5}\,\rm{M}_{\odot}$ where non-linearities become important. This model enables efficient field-level forward modelling for simulation-based inference and model comparison with large datasets from forthcoming galaxy surveys including Euclid, Rubin LSST, and Roman, while improving the accuracy of galaxy bias modelling with respect to standard linear deterministic models.

2610.12121.title: Too many or too bright? Status and perspectives in the study of the UV Luminosity Function at z>10
2610.12121.abstract: The finding that galaxies in the first 500Myr were much more numerous and/or brighter than expected is often cited as one of the main discoveries of the James Webb Space Telescope in its first four years of operation. This result is now solidly based on an impressive number of surveys that have detected, spectroscopically confirmed, and characterized a relatively large sample of galaxies up to z=14.44, the redshift of the most distant galaxy currently known. This finding has motivated the introduction of additional physical mechanisms into theoretical models to reproduce the observed numbers and luminosities. These results contrast with the failure, despite ongoing efforts, to confirm any galaxy candidate beyond this redshift. This review summarizes the status of the search for and characterization of galaxies at z>9, focusing on the evolution of the UV Luminosity Function (UVLF), which is the main statistical description of the galaxy population that can be obtained at these redshifts. We first provide a comprehensive overview of the full set of JWST data obtained so far. We perform a 'meta--analysis' on the entire data set and provide a simple yet effective description of the global evolution of the UVLF, averaging over the various surveys. We also compare these results extensively with theoretical models that were developed to match the new JWST observations and that explore different physical mechanisms able to drive the observed evolution. We conclude with a summary of the contrasting results regarding the search for galaxy candidates at z>15, and outline the requirements for future surveys aimed at breaking this barrier.

2610.11762.title: Probing Massive Star Formation with Intrinsic Multiplicity Constraints from TESS Eclipsing Binaries
2610.11762.abstract: Massive stars play a central role in stellar and galactic evolution as progenitors of supernovae, neutron stars, black holes, and gravitational wave sources. Despite their importance, the dominant formation mechanisms of massive binaries remain poorly constrained observationally. We aim to use a large, homogeneous sample of eclipsing binaries to observationally constrain binary formation across a wide range of primary masses and test predictions from various formation scenarios. We combine photometric time series data from TESS with distance measurements from Gaia DR3 and near infrared photometry from 2MASS to analyze an all-sky sample of eclipsing binaries. By accounting for observational and geometric selection effects, we derive bias corrected estimates of the binary fractions and orbital parameter distributions across different mass bins. We derive bias corrected binary fractions and bias corrected distributions of orbital period and radius-to-separation ratio for systems spanning primary masses from 1.1 Msun to 47 Msun. For primary masses up to 5 Msun, the observed distributions show close agreement with theoretical predictions for systems formed via disk fragmentation followed by migration. At higher masses, we observe an apparent deficit of very short period systems relative to theoretical expectations, although this regime is also expected to be affected by incompleteness. Overall, the observed properties exhibit a gradual transition across the full range of primary masses. Within the orbital period range accessible to our sample, the results do not require a sharp transition in binary properties between F- and O-type stars. The observed continuity is consistent with disk fragmentation followed by migration acting across a broad range of stellar masses, although the present data do not uniquely require this formation pathway and alternative channels may also contribute.

2610.12398.title: ACORN I. Massive Black Hole Seeding and Tidal Disruption Events from Star Clusters in Cosmological Simulations
2610.12398.abstract: JWST has revealed massive star clusters at $z\gtrsim 6$, which provide promising environments for massive black hole (MBH) seed formation. We introduce a new MBH seeding model for cosmological simulations, physically motivated by the runaway collisions in star clusters. Subgrid star clusters are generated according to the local ISM and evolved through stellar evolution and two-body relaxation. The masses of MBH seeds formed through runaway collisions are determined by the properties of their host clusters, including the effects of metallicity-dependent stellar winds. We further follow tidal disruption events (TDEs) with the evolving clusters, which can be enhanced in MBH binaries, and account for gravitational-wave (GW) recoil following MBH mergers. We implement this model in a constrained simulation of a 5$σ$ overdense region, where seeds of $10^{3}-10^{5.6}\,M_\odot$ form in clusters with $10^{4}\leq m_{\rm SC}\leq 10^{8}\,M_\odot$. Because both the seed abundance and mass are directly connected to the local environment, we have a more physical $M_{\rm BH}\!-\!M_{\rm galaxy}$ scaling for low-mass galaxies ($M_{\rm galaxy}\sim10^{6-9}\,M_\odot$), a regime poorly described by previous seeding models. Multiple MBHs are naturally allowed to form in-situ within individual halos, producing a spatially clustered population. This increases the MBH merger rate by $\sim100$ relative to other seeding models, significantly enhancing the expected LISA event rate. TDEs can dominate the growth of $10^{3-4}\,M_\odot$ MBHs and produce luminous flares of $L_{\rm peak}\sim 10^{42-43}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$, increasing the observability of low-mass seeds. This seeding prescription accelerates early MBH growth at $z\gtrsim 8$, while subsequent self-regulated gas accretion drives the central MBH toward similar masses $\sim10^{8.6}\, M_\odot$ by $z=6$ across different seeding models.

2610.14181.title: Globular cluster Observations for Luminosity-dispersion Distances (GOLD): Project description and velocity catalogue
2610.14181.abstract: We introduce and describe the Globular cluster Observations for Luminosity-Dispersion distances (GOLD) project, which has the principal aim of determining independent distances based on the globular cluster (GC) absolute magnitude-velocity dispersion ($M_V - σ$) relation calibrated with Milky Way GCs with Gaia distances. The project comprises observations of GCs in 19 early- and late-type galaxies taken with FLAMES/GIRAFFE on ESO's Very Large Telescope. So far, 17 galaxies have been observed. The spectra cover the wavelength range 8483-9000 AA, including the calcium triplet region at a spectral resolution of $R\sim18,000$. The spectra provide line-of-sight velocities with typical uncertainties of $Δv = 1-2$ km s$^{-1}$. Using primarily velocities to separate extragalactic sources from foreground stars, we present here our initial sample of 1062 GCs and 101 ultra-compact dwarf galaxies (UCDs). For more than 650 of these objects we present the first velocity measurement. We discuss the available photometry and size measurements, and show that our velocities are in good agreement with previous studies. Our velocity catalogues are made publicly available. Beyond the principal aim of obtaining precision distances, additional science to be explored with these data includes host galaxy halo dynamics and clustering analysis, mass-to light ratios of GCs and UCDs in the sample, the stellar initial mass function and black hole occupation fraction of the GCs, and chemical abundances from high-dispersion spectra.

2610.12562.title: The accretionally heated atmospheres of protoplanets and brown dwarfs
2610.12562.abstract: The ranks of accreting planets and brown dwarfs are growing. To help interpret their spectra, we study how accretion affects a planet's atmosphere. The atmosphere is irradiated from above by whatever nonthermal radiation from the accretion shock does not directly escape into space. This accretional heating drives a temperature inversion. Even relatively slow accretion, corresponding to mass doubling times longer than system ages, can raise temperatures by many hundreds of Kelvin at ambient pressures of order millibars. The heated atmosphere radiates an optical/infrared excess. For environments that are not too dusty, the excess concentrates in molecular lines that trace the heated layer. Thus an accretionally heated atmosphere may be distinguished by its muted absorption bands. Irradiation from the accretion shock also changes the chemical composition of the atmosphere, further altering spectra. Atmospheric retrievals promise to map out the deposition of accretional energy, helping to decide between ''hot'' and ''cold'' start modes of planet formation.

2610.13200.title: Detailed study of HD 219134: a benchmark K-dwarf with a compact planetary system
2610.13200.abstract: Space missions such as CoRoT, Kepler, and TESS have transformed asteroseismology and its synergies with exoplanet science. We revisit the nearby K-dwarf HD 219134 to investigate the tension between asteroseismic and interferometric radii, update its fundamental parameters, and reconstruct the rotational, magnetic, and atmospheric evolution of the system. We combine forward asteroseismic modeling with seismic inversions to assess systematics from non-seismic constraints, radius measurements, and surface modeling. The revised stellar properties are then used for rotational evolution, stellar-wind, and high-energy irradiation calculations. Seismic inversions rule out the most recent interferometric radius, while the asteroseismic and spectroscopic results are compatible with the 2019 interferometric measurement. We obtain $M=0.779\pm0.015_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.006_\mathrm{(sys)}\ M_\odot$, $R=0.753\pm0.005_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.002_\mathrm{(sys)}\ R_\odot$, and an age of $8.92\pm0.89_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.19_\mathrm{(sys)}$ Gyr. These systematics include only non-seismic constraints; literature combined uncertainties from physical inputs and surface effects are $0.007M_\odot$, $0.002R_\odot$, and $0.81$ Gyr. Rotational and wind modelling shows that standard magnetic braking is broadly compatible with the present-day rotation and angular-momentum loss. Weakened braking gives a closer match but challenges standard wind-loss scalings. The inferred X-ray history suggests early stripping of the innermost planets, while the outer planets likely retained part of their primordial envelopes; HD 219134d experienced only moderate erosion. The apparent radius discrepancy likely reflects underestimated uncertainties in previous interferometric analyses rather than an astrophysical inconsistency. We advocate adopting the asteroseismic radius, which is robust to modeling assumptions and optimisation strategies.

2610.11203.title: Pinpointing the cosmic web between massive galaxy clusters I. The incidence of HI and OVI as WHIM tracers
2610.11203.abstract: At redshift z<1, the $Λ$CDM paradigm predicts that $\sim$40-50\% of baryons reside in the warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM) within cosmic web filaments. Characterizing the physical state and distribution of this dominant baryonic component is crucial for a complete picture of baryon evolution in the low-redshift Universe. However, directly observing the WHIM has been challenging due to its low density and high temperature and ionization state. Absorption-line spectroscopy offers a promising approach, particularly through analyses of broad Ly-$α$ absorbers (BLAs; Doppler parameter b>40 km/s) and OVI absorbers. This work focuses on probing WHIM signatures by analyzing the incidence rates of these tracers in and around putative cosmic web filaments connecting massive galaxy clusters. We use far-ultraviolet (FUV) absorption spectroscopy from HST/COS along ten QSO sightlines at z<1, selected for their proximity in projected distance and velocity to cluster pairs. We focus on absorption features of WHIM tracers (BLAs and OVI) and cold-gas tracers (narrow Ly-$α$ absorbers, or NLAs; b<40 km/s), which are used as a control sample for colder gas. We measure excess incidence rates for total HI, NLAs, BLAs, and OVI within a rest-frame $Δv=\pm1000$ km/s and an impact parameter $Δd<3$ Mpc relative to the field expectation, and find that the excesses of BLAs and OVI are about twice those of NLAs. Additionally, the covering fractions of BLAs and OVI appear larger by factors of $\sim$1.7 and 1.8, respectively, than in a random field control sample, whereas the NLA covering fraction is consistent with the random expectation. The larger relative excess of WHIM tracers compared to cold-gas tracers near independent cluster pairs indicates the prevalence of warm-hot gas in these environments, representing a potential signature of WHIM detection in inter-cluster filaments.

2610.14167.title: Where Cluster Galaxies Reside and How Strongly They Lens
2610.14167.abstract: The efficiency of galaxy-galaxy strong lensing (GGSL) in clusters depends jointly on the inner mass distributions of member galaxies and their locations within the cluster potential. Observed GGSL probabilities exceed $Λ$CDM predictions by nearly an order of magnitude, but the relative roles of internal structure and environment remain unclear. We disentangle these effects by comparing HST strong-lensing clusters with TNG-Cluster analogs at similar lens redshifts, matched by their primary Einstein radius. For each member, we measure its lensing strength in isolation and when embedded in the cluster field. Members in cluster-critical regions are classified as Major or Minor Perturbers depending on whether they strongly lens in isolation; those in subcritical regions are classified as Intrinsic Lenses, Boosted Lenses, or Inert Members according to whether they lens independently, only with environmental assistance, or not at all. Observed clusters contain 33.7% of selected members in cluster-critical regions, compared with 21.6% in TNG-Cluster, while their Major-to-Minor ratios are similar. Outside these regions, observations contain substantially more Intrinsic and Boosted Lenses and fewer Inert Members, with Boosted Lens fractions of 25.8% and 13.5%, respectively. The discrepancy persists at fixed subhalo mass and after including line-of-sight structure. A mass-conserving contraction mimicking core-collapsed self-interacting dark matter largely recovers the conditional lensing fractions but not cluster-critical occupancy. The GGSL discrepancy therefore reflects both insufficient central concentration in simulated members and differences in their locations within the cluster lensing field.

2610.13726.title: Turbulence modes in molecular clouds in M33: a challenging test of the Brunt-Federrath framework
2610.13726.abstract: Understanding the turbulent structure of molecular clouds is essential for linking galactic environment to the regulation of star formation. Although Galactic molecular clouds have been studied extensively, extending turbulence-mode analysis beyond the Milky Way remains challenging because of the limited spatial resolution and dynamic range of extragalactic observations. We assess the applicability of the Brunt \& Federrath (2014; BF14) framework to molecular clouds in M33. We apply BF14 to 128 $^{13}$CO(2-1) clouds, selecting a primary quality-controlled sample of 54 clouds and a more restrictive 25-cloud subsample defined using a stricter extraction-padding criterion (PAD=2) for quantitative analysis.Tests of cloud and noise power spectra, Fourier-space cutoffs, extraction padding, and Monte Carlo uncertainties demonstrate that the retained spatial frequencies are dominated by astrophysical signal and that the inferred turbulence-mode fractions are robust against reasonable analysis choices. Both samples yield consistent distributions of the solenoidal fraction, with mean values of $R \simeq 0.22$ for both samples and median values of $R \simeq 0.18$ and $0.17$, respectively, indicating that compressive motions dominate the turbulent energy budget. No strong systematic variations of $R$ are found with galactocentric distance or tracers of recent star formation. These results demonstrate that, despite the challenging spatial resolution of current extragalactic molecular-line observations, the BF14 framework can be applied reliably to nearby galaxies using spectroscopic observations alone. To our knowledge, this constitutes the first application of the full BF14 formalism to extragalactic molecular-cloud observations.

2610.11102.title: The Binary Fraction of Milky Way Field Stars in DESI: Dependence on Chemical Abundance
2610.11102.abstract: Binary populations encode information about the physical conditions of star formation and the subsequent evolution of stellar populations. Adopting a statistical method based on multi-epoch line-of-sight velocity variations, we constrain the binary fraction, $f_b$, of field main-sequence turn-off stars in the Milky Way using data from the second data release of the DESI Milky Way Survey. $f_b$ is found to primarily increase with lower [Fe/H]. At $[\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{H}]\gtrsim -1.3$, $f_b$ shows a modest increase with increasing [Mg/Fe], whereas no clear trend is detected at lower [Fe/H]. The apparent variations of $f_b$ with angular momentum and Galactic height are largely explained by their underlying [Fe/H] distributions, while the remaining variations broadly follow differences in [Mg/Fe]. Within overlapping regions of the [Fe/H]--[Mg/Fe] plane, the thin disk, thick disk, stellar halo and GSE populations exhibit no significant differences in their binary fractions. Thus, our measurements indicate that the variation in $f_b$ is dominated by chemical abundance, which could be explained by the metallicity-dependent gas cooling efficiency and fragmentation. The weaker [Mg/Fe] dependence at fixed [Fe/H] might be associated with the formation conditions of stars, with higher [Mg/Fe] stars generally forming earlier under a more gas-rich and turbulent environment.

2610.12143.title: Discovery of the Slowest Radio Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud
2610.12143.abstract: We report the discovery of a new radio pulsar PSR J0103$-$72 in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) through a reanalysis of Parkes/Murriyang archival observations targeting supernova remnants and pulsar-wind nebulae in the SMC. Previously two pulsars were discovered in these observations, and PSR J0103$-$72 is the third which we independently detected in two observations of its target field. It has a spin period of 1.327 sec and a dispersion measure (DM) of $272\pm13~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, making it the slowest known radio pulsar in the SMC with the second-highest DM. We did not identify any plausible supernova remnant or pulsar-wind nebula associated with the pulsar. Subtracting the predicted Galactic foreground leaves a DM contribution of $\sim 230$--$242~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, which may suggest a long path through the ionized medium of the SMC, enhanced ionized gas along the sightline, or both. Although these data had previously been searched using both FFT and fast folding algorithms, our FFT-based reprocessing found PSR J0103$-$72 through search techniques which have previously been highly effective in discovering a large number of pulsars in other surveys. This discovery shows that candidates with weak Fourier-domain significance can reveal faint, narrow-duty cycle pulsars missed in earlier extragalactic pulsar searches.

2610.35917.title: The [Y/Mg] chemical clock and the stellar ages of solar-type stars in the solar neighbourhood
2610.35917.abstract: Stellar ages are an important parameter for studying the chemical evolution of the Galaxy. To improve age estimates, various complementary methods to the conventional isochrone-fitting method have been implemented in the last decade. The [Y/Mg] ratio has been proposed as a chemical clock for solar-metallicity stars, due to its strong dependence on stellar age. In this work, we study the behaviour of the abundance ratio [Y/Mg] in metal-poor stars, along with other solar-type disk stars, as a function of stellar age determined through isochrones. The analysis is based on the line-by-line differential technique, applied to a sample covering a wide metallicity range ($-$0.70 $\leq$ [Fe/H] $<$ +0.34), using high-resolution (R = 115,000) and high S/N spectra (= 270 - 1000) taken with the HARPS spectrograph at the ESO La Silla Observatory. We find that the stellar sample follows a metallicity-dependent [Y/Mg]-Age relation.

2610.12158.title: HI intensity mapping with MeerKAT: A measurement of the 21-cm auto-spectrum on cosmological scales
2610.12158.abstract: We report a direct measurement of the 21-cm signal from neutral hydrogen (HI) via the intensity mapping technique at redshift $z = 0.42$ through its power spectrum at cosmological scales $0.095\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}<k<0.245\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We analyse intensity maps observed in the frequency range $971.2\,{\rm MHz}<ν<1023.6\,{\rm MHz}$ during the 2021 observational campaign of the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) spanning an area of approximately $236\,{\rm deg}^2$. Capitalising on the depth of this survey, we divide the data set into multiple observationally independent subsets. After performing blind contaminant separation independently on each subset, we exploit internal cross-correlations to suppress the instrumental noise plateau and isolate the cosmological signal from residual systematics. Although the subsets' auto-spectra show the presence of excess power that we deem linked to still unresolved systematics, the cross-spectra measurements satisfactorily pass a battery of null and robustness tests. We introduce a multi-subset formalism to infer the amplitude of the HI auto-spectrum from our internal cross-spectra measurements while marginalising the potential signal loss that occurs during data processing, reaching a detection with signal-to-noise ratio of 6.2. We constrain the clustering amplitude of the signal in terms of the HI cosmic abundance and its linear bias, measuring $10^3\,Ω_{\rm HI} b_{\rm HI}=1.271^{+1.080}_{-0.598}$. This direct measurement marks a milestone in demonstrating the effectiveness of the HI intensity mapping technique for future surveys with the SKA Observatory, of which MeerKAT is a precursor.

2610.12322.title: JWST CAPERS: Spectroscopic evaluation of very high redshift galaxy candidates
2610.12322.abstract: JWST/NIRCam imaging has enabled efficient selection of a large number of galaxy candidates at very high redshifts. Accurate and robust selection is crucial for statistical analyses, such as measurement of the ultraviolet luminosity function (UV LF). A variety of selection methods and criteria have been proposed in the literature. We evaluate the selection methodology of galaxy candidates at $z\geq8.5$ using 183 candidates with secure spectroscopic redshifts obtained from the CAPERS JWST/NIRSpec PRISM program. The success of high-$z$ confirmation is strongly correlated with the photometric signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in the detection filter, the strength of the Lyman-$α$ break, and the $Δχ^2$ between the best-fitting low-redshift and high-redshift spectral energy distribution model. However, the most efficient selection method is the use of a UV LF prior on the inferred $p(z)$ of a source, raising the success rate from $\simeq 35\%$ to $\simeq 77\%$ while achieving greater completeness than conservative SNR and $Δχ^2$ cuts. Out of the 183 candidates we spectroscopically confirm 48 sources at $z\geq8.5$ via detections of emission lines and/or the Lyman-$α$ break (particularly important for those with no emission line detection). We report the highest-redshift source in CAPERS as UDS-111893 at $z_{\mathrm{spec}}=12.98$, with no sources confirmed at $z>13$. This work provides spectroscopic quantification of JWST/NIRCam photometric selection at $z\geq8.5$, and demonstrates the effectiveness of a UV LF prior for high-redshift photometric selection.

2610.13942.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
2610.13942.abstract: To search for very wide-orbit binary-lens events, we cross-match microlensing events detected by OGLE-IV and KMTNet between 2011 and 2024. After removing contaminants from variable stars, we identify OGLE-2016-BLG-0523 as a microlensing event showing two short-lived bumps in its light curve, with the two separated by 8.36 yr. We investigate three scenarios to explain the two bumps, including a binary-lens single-source (2L1S), a single-lens binary-source (1L2S), and two unrelated single-lens single-source events (2$\times$1L1S). The 1L2S interpretation is excluded due to its poorer fit to the data, while the 2$\times$1L1S scenario is disfavored by the low event rate, unphysical total source flux, and unphysical color for one of the two putative sources. For the surviving 2L1S interpretation, the Einstein timescales of the two bumps are $8.343 \pm 0.076$ days and $3.231 \pm 0.047$ days, respectively, implying a binary mass ratio of $q = 0.15$. A Bayesian analysis indicates that the primary lens is most likely a low-mass M dwarf, while the companion is probably a low-mass brown dwarf or super-Jupiter. The inferred projected separation is about 450 au, making the companion the widest low-mass object discovered via microlensing to date. Our discovery highlights both the promise and challenges of identifying very wide, low-mass companions through microlensing. Although upcoming facilities such as Roman and Earth 2.0 space telescopes will improve sensitivity to such events, overcoming degeneracies and distinguishing them from variable phenomena will remain essential for building a robust statistical sample.

2610.11949.title: Testing General Relativity with Binary Lens Microlensing Events
2610.11949.abstract: Einstein's General Relativity (GR), which has been precisely tested on galaxy and solar system scales, is still poorly constrained in extremely weak gravitational fields (with dimensionless Newtonian potentials of $Φ\sim 10^{-8}$). In this Letter, we propose a new method to probe such a weak-field regime of gravity and measure the spatial curvature generated per unit mass. Specifically, binary microlensing events provide a laboratory to measure the parameterized post-Newtonian (PPN) parameter ($γ$), by combining the lensing mass ($M_{\rm lens}^{\rm GR}$) inferred from microlensing with the dynamical mass ($M_{\rm dyn}$) determined from interferometric astrometry. Astrometric tracking of binary lenses was previously hindered by their faintness and minuscule angular separations (typically a few milliarcseconds). This limitation has been alleviated by the deployment of GRAVITY+, which pushes the instrument's sensitivity and astrometric precision to unprecedented heights. Based on astrometric simulations of the binary microlensing event ASASSN-22av, we directly estimate $γ$ at the precision of ~23%. Such test of GR in the extremely weak-field regime can be further improved to much higher precision (~3%), based on more binary microlensing events with precise determination of the dynamical/lens mass.

2610.12117.title: EWOCS-XI: Anisotropic expansion and shear in the cluster Westerlund 1. A 2D kinematic analysis with Gaia DR3
2610.12117.abstract: Westerlund 1 (Wd1) is one of the Milky Way's most massive young clusters, in which heavy extinction and field contamination have historically hampered its kinematic characterization. We aim to assess Wd1's internal kinematics, dynamical state, and formation scenario. Using a robust 5D clustering approach, we identified 559 bona fide members. We modeled their proper motions via a 2D first-order Taylor expansion to derive the velocity gradient tensor, mapping expansion, rotation, and shear. Restricting the kinematic analysis to 524 stars with proper motion uncertainties $<0.5~\mathrm{mas\,yr^{-1}}$, we find at least 103 gravitationally unbound members, including 14 walkaway stars. The 2D analysis reveals a statistically significant divergence (>4$σ$) highlighting preferred expansion along the Galactic latitude (position angle $164^\circ\pm10.1^\circ$). A detected cross-gradient ($\partial v_b / \partial l = -0.41 \pm 0.08$ km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{-1}$) provides a clear signature of shear on the plane of the sky. Wd1 does not behave as a single cohesive population, but comprises two decoupled subsystems: a stable, bound core in dynamical equilibrium and an escaping, unbound envelope. This prominent anisotropic expansion perpendicular to the Galactic plane has a kinematic timescale ($Δt_{\mathrm{kin}} = 2.08 \pm 0.44$ Myr) matching the independent orbital mid-plane crossing time ($Δt_{\mathrm{orbit}} = 2.10 \pm 0.05$ Myr). This temporal alignment indicates the expansion onset coincided with Wd1's Galactic disk passage, triggered either by internal dynamics (e.g., early supernova feedback) or external tidal perturbations. Finally, the robust unbound population demonstrates that active cluster dissolution is underway, driven by discrete dynamical ejection events rather than long-term stellar evaporation.

2610.11530.title: Gaseous SiO and Silicate Clouds in Three Benchmark Early-L Dwarfs
2610.11530.abstract: Tracing silicon from gaseous SiO into silicate condensates provides a direct view of the condensation process that forms silicate clouds in L-dwarf atmospheres. Here we present evidence for gaseous SiO in three benchmark early-L dwarfs, HD 89744B, GJ 1048B, and LSPM J0632+5053B, using JWST/NIRSpec and MIRI spectroscopy. Atmospheric retrievals with and without SiO under multiple cloud prescriptions identify the strongest SiO signatures at 4.0--4.2 and 7.7--8.2 $μ$m, with the local likelihood diagnostic reaching $4.6σ$. In the physical cloud retrievals, the 8 $μ$m band probes lower pressures than the 4 $μ$m overtone, reaching atmospheric layers where equilibrium SiO is more strongly depleted by silicate condensation. All three objects also show compact Fe opacity at pressures of a few bar. Their inferred gas-phase C/O ratios are consistent with expectations from the host-star compositions after accounting for refractory oxygen sequestration. Within the adopted Mie treatment of amorphous silicate grains, the silicate mineralogies favor Mg$_2$SiO$_4$ for HD 89744B and a mixed Mg$_2$SiO$_4$+MgSiO$_3$ cloud for GJ 1048B. Extending this framework to cooler L dwarfs will trace the coupled evolution of gaseous SiO depletion and silicate-cloud formation along the L-dwarf sequence.

2610.13062.title: A Relationship Between Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure and Host Galaxy Inclination
2610.13062.abstract: It is commonly thought that fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace star formation, and that they are produced by magnetars. Both hypotheses imply that their sources are hosted primarily (but not exclusively) in galactic disks. Although there is evidence in that direction, it has yet to be shown conclusively. In addition, a tension exists with the fact that at least one FRB source is found in a globular cluster far from the disk of the host. If FRBs originate primarily in disks, the galaxy orientation could leave an impression in the sample of observed FRBs, either as a selection bias against FRBs in edge-on galaxies or as a correlation with DMHost. Statistical tests against the inclinations of FRB host galaxies, derived from parametric morphology applied to optical and near-infrared imaging, can search for these effects. Such a search requires an adequately large sample of known FRB hosts that have been imaged to a sufficient depth, while estimates of DMHost also require the redshift of each host to be known. These conditions are best met in the Commensal Real-time ASKAP Fast Transient (CRAFT) survey sample of FRB host galaxies, for which the majority have been imaged at optical wavelengths with FORS2 on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). Here these data are fitted with the morphology software GALFIT to derive the elliptical axis ratio q (a proxy for inclination) for 34 hosts from the CRAFT sample, detected with ASKAP and followed up with VLT imaging. We find no bias against FRB detections from edge-on galaxies; instead, we uncover a new relationship between the inclination of an FRB host galaxy and DMHost. This is consistent with a primarily disk-based origin for CRAFT FRBs. Using this relationship we are able to reduce the scatter of the host sample about the Macquart relation by 40%, demonstrating a new empirical method for estimating DMHost that requires only deep optical imaging.

2610.13492.title: An empirical calibration of the spectral resolution of JWST NIRSpec PRISM
2610.13492.abstract: We present an empirical calibration of the effective spectral resolution of the JWST NIRSpec PRISM disperser based on a large sample of galaxies drawn from archival observations. Our sample spans a wide redshift range, $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 10$, enabling a wavelength-dependent characterization of the PRISM resolving power across the full bandpass using the [O III]$λ\lambda4959,5007$ doublets. To ensure robust measurements, we impose strict signal-to-noise requirements on both continuum and emission-line detections. Emission-line profiles are fitted with multi-Gaussian models, and the full width at half maximum (FWHM) is measured for each source. The derived empirical resolution curve shows a systematic offset from the nominal pre-launch estimate, lying between the tabulated instrumental resolution and the point-source shutter limit. We also discuss how source size affects the final spectral resolution, and provide an analytical formula that combines wavelength and morphology dependence in a root-sum-square framework. This work delivers a population-averaged, statistically robust calibration of the effective PRISM spectral resolution for typical galaxy observations. The resulting calibration is directly applicable to statistical analyses of galaxy spectra obtained with NIRSpec PRISM. Our empirical calibration exceeds the pre-launch JDox values by a factor of 1.03 to 1.63, depending on source morphology, and provides the first wavelength and morphology dependent calibration of the NIRSpec PRISM spectral resolution.

2610.14371.title: TESS Pulsation Timing Reveals the JWST Calibration Star HD 158485 as a Double-pulsator Binary
2610.14371.abstract: HD~158485 is an A-type $δ$~Scuti star in the CALSPEC network and the JWST absolute-flux calibration program. Gaia DR3 assigns it a binary classification probability close to unity but provides no orbital solution. Using TESS observations from Sectors 14--26, 40--41, 47--60, and 73--86, we measure the pulsation phases of six $δ$~Scuti modes. The frequencies form two groups with opposite light-travel-time delays, revealing two pulsating components. A direct light-curve forward model yields an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb}=382.80^{+0.80}_{-0.76}$~d, eccentricity $e=0.242^{+0.045}_{-0.046}$, projected light-time amplitudes of $195.8^{+9.2}_{-8.9}$ and $239.7^{+6.8}_{-6.8}$~s, and a dynamical mass ratio of $q=M_B/M_A=0.818^{+0.046}_{-0.045}$. A blind prediction based only on the first two long TESS campaigns reproduces the third campaign without updating the orbital parameters, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of $r=0.983$. Its held-out rms is 83.8~s, compared with 289.9~s when the period is fixed at 365.25~d. A 5.15-$σ$ Hipparcos--Gaia EDR3 proper-motion anomaly independently indicates unresolved astrometric motion. The unresolved companion can also affect spectrophotometric predictions: a conditional PB2-constrained two-atmosphere model differs from the corresponding single-star atmosphere prediction by 1.6\% over 1--5~$μ$m and 2.5\% over 5--28~$μ$m. HD~158485 therefore shows that a calibration-relevant binary can lack a catalogued orbital solution while two independent pulsation clocks reveal and measure its orbit.

2610.14283.title: What does self-supervision add to engineered features for stellar light curves?
2610.14283.abstract: TESS light curves encode a star's pulsation, rotation, binarity and oscillations, among other physical properties, but the survey produces far more light curves than can be labelled by hand. Astronomers have engineered a few dozen physically motivated features from them, which together remain a strong baseline. Previous work has trained encoders on light curves and judged them by their own downstream scores, but has not asked what they add to the engineered features. We pre-train a convolutional encoder on unlabelled TESS light curves to predict each window's latent representation from those of its neighbours. We then freeze it, add its features to the 25 engineered features, and read the combination out with one fixed linear probe on ten tasks: five variability classes, four asteroseismic targets and rotation period. Adding the learned features improves the readout on 7 of 10 tasks over the engineered features alone, where an untrained encoder does not. The combination also outperforms two networks trained end-to-end on the same labelled stars on most tasks. An encoder trained without labels therefore gives astronomers new features that complement the ones they already use rather than replace them.

2610.14353.title: The effect of triples on the Chemically Homogeneous Evolution Channel for producing Gravitational Wave Sources
2610.14353.abstract: Despite the growing number of gravitational-wave (GW) detections, the formation of merging binary black holes (BBHs) is still debated. One of the proposed formation channels is Chemically Homogeneous Evolution (CHE), which makes distinct predictions for the properties of the resulting black holes (BHs): high masses ($\gtrsim35\, M_\odot$) and large, orbitally-aligned spins. These predictions are based on studies that consider this channel only in isolated binaries. However, most massive stars reside in triples. We investigate how a tertiary affects the CHE channel. We use detailed binary models computed with MESA for the inner CHE systems coupled with analytical prescriptions for the hierarchical triple dynamics. Specifically, we study the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai mechanism that can accelerate the merger of the inner BBHs through high-eccentricity excitations. We show that a tertiary companion enables mergers at higher metallicities, where the classical binary CHE channel does not operate. At $Z_\odot/3$, triples produce BHs with lower masses (around $15\,M_\odot$) and lower spins (around 0.25) compared to the low-metallicity classical scenario. We further expect triple dynamics to lead to spin-orbit misalignment and potential residual eccentricities at merger. In triples at $Z_\odot/3$, half of the mergers occur within 1 Gyr. Moreover, 10% of the population leads to prompt mergers within 1 Myr (1% within 1 kyr) that are of potential interest for electromagnetic counterparts. We conclude that the triple CHE channel is promising as (i) it may contribute more substantially to the local merger rate than had been expected for the classical CHE channel due to the shorter delay times and effectiveness at higher metallicities and (ii) produces mergers with properties that more closely resemble the lower masses and lower spins inferred for most of the observed GW merger population.

2610.14172.title: A first view of interstellar Fe-bearing dust grains with XRISM
2610.14172.abstract: Understanding the reservoirs of iron (Fe) in our Galaxy is crucial for probing the mechanisms that drive dust grain growth in the interstellar medium (ISM). High-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy offers a powerful tool to investigate the chemistry of dust grains, particularly those containing Fe, through spectroscopic features near photoabsorption edges known as X-ray Absorption Fine Structures (XAFS). With the Resolve spectrometer aboard XRISM, we can now examine the Fe K-edge (7.1 keV) owing to its improved spectral resolution in this energy range. This enabled us to probe the dust grain chemistry in high Galactic column densities. In this work, we present a pilot study on dust grain chemistry through the Fe K-edge of the XRISM Performance Verification target GX 340+0. This source is a persistently bright low-mass X-ray binary with a hydrogen column density of 6.6x10^22 cm^-2 along the line of sight, providing sufficient optical depth at the Fe K-edge. By fitting combined dust and gas models, we find that Fe is depleted by 95% into dust along the line of sight towards the source. Moreover, we find evidence that 38% of the solid-phase Fe is in metallic iron, 47% in iron sulfides, and the remainder in silicates. The large contribution from metallic iron and iron sulfides differs from what is typically inferred from X-ray studies of diffuse ISM and may suggest that that these compounds become more significant reservoirs of Fe in higher column density Galactic sightlines.

2610.13393.title: Detecting redshift space distortions with forthcoming 21cm intensity maps from MeerKLASS
2610.13393.abstract: Redshift space distortions (RSD) provide a powerful measurement of structure formation in modern cosmology. In this work, we explore the potential of 21cm intensity mapping with the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) to detect RSD and probe gravity within the redshift range of MeerKAT's UHF band ($0.4<z<1.45$). Using simulated sky observations, we examine the impact from observational effects caused by blind foreground removal and MeerKAT's primary beam, plus $k$-cuts to the measurements. With a multipole expansion formalism, we demonstrate how the quadrupole of the HI power spectrum can be modelled and also show how a foreground transfer function can reconstruct the distorted signal. With 1,115 deg$^2$ of simulated MeerKLASS observations at $0.4<z<1.0$, our proposed analysis pipeline reveals a $6.7σ$ detection of an RSD-induced quadrupole relative to one caused by anisotropic observational effects alone. We also explore parameter inference with the full MeerKLASS 10,000 deg$^2$ survey. Within forecasts, we demonstrate how a tomographic analysis across the full UHF redshift range can be leveraged to address certain parameter degeneracies with e.g. the HI bias ($b_{\rm HI}$) and cosmic density of HI ($Ω_{\rm HI}$). By adopting a redshift-dependent model for the bias and HI density combined with simulation-informed priors, we demonstrate how degeneracies can be alleviated, and indicate the potential for MeerKLASS to reach competitive precision on simple probes of modified gravity.

2610.12553.title: A Single Line-Emitter Identified in an Unbiased Search with JWST/NIRSpec: Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy
2610.12553.abstract: We report the detection of a previously unknown object with a single emission line within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, using a new JWST NIRSpec technique called Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy (MOCSS) with the G140M/F100LP observing mode. The MOCSS technique involves opening almost all the shutters on the NIRSpec microshutter array, while simultaneously closing the shutters that lie on top of known low redshift objects, facilitating a wide field slitless spectroscopic search without contamination from bright objects. This observational technique has enabled the detection of a strong emission line in four different dither positions and in two position angles, and thus cannot be artificial. This line is detected at 1.60 $\rm μm$ with a line flux of $[2.5\pm 0.3]\times10^{-18} \rm erg\ s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and a FWHM of $13.2\pm2.0$Å, and does not correspond to any known source with some of the deepest HST and JWST imaging in existence. Based upon the absence of imaging detection, we place a lower limit on the observed frame equivalent width (EW) of 7620Å on this object, which strongly limits the number of possible lines that this line can be. Given the wavelength, an EW limit that is near the ceiling of expectation, and the lack of other lines in the bandpass, this line cannot be easily explained by [OII] at $z=3.29$, [OIII] at $z=2.20$, H$α$ at $z=1.44$, and Ly$α$ at $z=12.16$. We discuss possible AGN and transient phenomena that could explain the finding.

2610.14348.title: Mapping Wolf-Rayet winds with spectro-interferometry I. Detection of multiple co-rotating interaction regions in WR 6
2610.14348.abstract: WR 6 is the prototype for periodic variability due to large-scale wind structures in Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars, showing a consistent periodicity of 3.76 d in photometry, spectroscopy, and polarimetry. However, the origin of this variability is debated, attributed either to corotating interaction regions (CIRs) or a low-mass companion. We use time-resolved interferometry to investigate the origin of periodic variability in WR 6. We aim to detect and characterize structures in the stellar winds of WR 6 and discriminate between the CIR and low-mass companion scenarios. Using the extended configuration of the Auxiliary Telescopes at VLTI, we obtained six GRAVITY epochs over six months to search for the presence and variability of wind-structures in WR 6. We also obtained complementary spectroscopic observations during one of the epochs to monitor contemporaneous spectral line variability. For all six epochs of GRAVITY observations: (i) WR 6 is consistent with a single star and has no spatially resolved companion detected above $M\gtrsim6\,M_\odot$; (ii) The He I line-emitting region is spatially resolved, while the He II lines remain unresolved, consistent with atmosphere models; (iii) Around 2.19 $μ$m, discrete line-emitting features offset from the center of the star are detected. The number, positions, and wavelengths of these features vary across epochs. Spectroscopic monitoring reveals spectral line residuals that broadly correspond to the two features seen in the GRAVITY data of the fifth epoch. Finally, the first three epochs, observed on three consecutive nights, show significant variability in these features but cannot be directly linked across epochs. We thus report the detection of multiple large-scale structures in the wind of WR 6 with VLTI/GRAVITY. We favor CIRs as their likely origin owing to temporal and spatial variability that cannot be reconciled with a low-mass companion.

2610.11985.title: Gas-phase chemistry of $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_3^+$: a key building block for carbon mass growth in space
2610.11985.abstract: The gas-phase chemistry of $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_3^+$ plays a central role in the growth of carbonaceous species across a wide range of environments, from combustion systems to interstellar media. However, the presence of multiple isomers, primarily the linear propargyl cation and the cyclic cyclopropenyl cation, has so far prevented the determination of reliable isomer-specific reaction kinetics. In this work, we combine tunable vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) photoionization with controlled ion--molecule reaction measurements to selectively produce and probe the reactivity of $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_3^+$ isomers. By employing a titration approach, we extract isomer-specific reaction rate coefficients and branching ratios for reactions of $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_3^+$ with $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4$, $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_4$, and $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6$. Our results demonstrate a strong contrast in reactivity: the most stable cyclic isomer is found to be essentially unreactive under the investigated conditions, whereas the linear isomer exhibits efficient and diverse chemistry leading to the formation of larger hydrocarbon ions. In particular, the formation of $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5^+$ is observed, providing an important intermediate in pathways toward aromatic species. These findings help resolve long-standing ambiguities in previously reported rate coefficients and provide new quantitative constraints for kinetic and astrochemical models. More broadly, this work highlights the importance of isomer-specific chemistry in carbon growth processes and demonstrates the effectiveness of VUV-based photoionization methods for disentangling complex reaction networks in the gas phase.

2610.13758.title: A dust-reddened quasar in a [C II]-luminous host at z=6.55
2610.13758.abstract: Most known quasars at $z>6$ were selected through their rest-frame UV emission. Only a small number of reddened quasars have been identified at these redshifts, leaving their nuclear and host-galaxy properties poorly constrained. We present JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy and ALMA band 6 observations of the quasar J1440+0019 at $z=6.5488$, revealing its dust-reddened nature and jointly characterizing its nucleus and host galaxy. The continuum is best described by an SMC-like extinction law with $E(B-V)=0.20\pm0.03$. Three absorption systems detected in N V, Si IV, and C IV are blueshifted by approximately $900$--$3600$ km s$^{-1}$ and likely trace an ionized nuclear outflow. The broad Mg II line and extinction-corrected continuum yield a black-hole mass of $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=9.04\pm0.42$, a bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm bol}\simeq1.1\times10^{47}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and an Eddington ratio of $λ_{\rm Edd}\simeq0.8$. ALMA observations further reveal its host galaxy to be among the most [C II]-luminous known at $z>6$, with $L_{\mathrm{[C II]}}=(7.21\pm0.25)\times10^9 L_\odot$. For a fiducial dust temperature of 47 K and emissivity index $β=1.6$, the dust continuum implies $L_{\rm TIR}=8.9\times10^{12} L_\odot$ and $M_{\rm dust}=4.0\times10^8 M_\odot$. The inferred dynamical mass places J1440+0019 in the region of the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm dyn}$ plane occupied by high-redshift blue quasars. These observations reveal a moderately reddened, rapidly accreting quasar in a luminous, dust-rich host during reionization. Its measured nuclear and host-galaxy properties provide an observational reference for identifying and characterizing similar systems in future systematic searches with wide-area infrared surveys.

2610.11045.title: Galaxy Clustering Can Reveal Host-Galaxy Properties of Binary Black Hole Mergers
2610.11045.abstract: Galaxy clustering encodes information about the host galaxies of binary black hole (BBH) mergers even when individual hosts remain unidentified, because the distribution of neighboring galaxies depends statistically on the host-galaxy population. We construct event-level host-type likelihoods from host-conditioned galaxy-count distributions within gravitational-wave localization regions and combine them to infer the fractions of BBH mergers hosted by different galaxy populations. The framework applies to common and rare galaxy populations without prescribing formation efficiencies or merger delay-time distributions. Using measured star-forming and quenched galaxy clustering, idealized one-year forecasts assuming all mergers occur in quenched galaxies yield median one-sided 90% lower credible limits of 0.19, 0.48, and 0.92 on the quenched-host fraction for O5, post-O5, and third-generation networks. These forecasts illustrate the potential for host-galaxy population inference before the third-generation detector era.

2610.11799.title: What powers the most energetic flares in the Kepler field? Revisiting the superflaring star KIC 2852961
2610.11799.abstract: Flare activity in red giants is quite common when continuously monitored with high-precision space photometry. In fact, the most powerful flares, also known as "superflares" have been observed on red giant stars. KIC 2852961 is a red giant star producing the highest-energy flares in the Kepler field, and is also known for its large-amplitude starspot-induced light variations. Our goal is to find out what causes the extreme flare activity and flare energies in this star. For our investigations, we use ground-based spectroscopic measurements and space photometric data, which we process using standard tools. We also collect relevant data from databases of large surveys such as Gaia. Our new radial velocity data confirm that the red giant star is part of a close binary system, in which tidal forces play a crucial role in controlling the evolution of the binary system. Our results show that tidal evolution has driven the system close to orbital circularization and rotational synchronization, but it did not completely constrain the differential rotation of the red giant, in which the magnetic dynamo can operate extremely efficiently. We find that high-energy (super)flares are primarily controlled by the internal magnetic activity of the active giant component, rather than phase-dependent interactions with the secondary star. The large spot-induced rotational light modulations indicate extensive starspots that can store enormous amounts of magnetic energy. This provides the conditions for the formation of extremely large flares, confirming the close relationship between large spot coverage and high flare energies and/or frequency. Behind all this, differential rotation may play a dual role in the flare activity of KIC 2852961: it contributes both to the formation of large starspots and to the shearing and twisting of coronal magnetic fields that can power energetic superflares.

2610.11541.title: Isotopic ratios as probes of star formation and the origin of molecular gas in the Central Molecular Zone
2610.11541.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) contains most of the dense molecular gas in the Milky Way but forms stars at a surprisingly low rate. Isotopic ratios provide a unique tool to investigate both the local physical conditions and the nucleosynthetic history of this gas. I summarize recent isotopic studies toward the molecular cloud G$+$0.693$-$0.027. Deuterium fractionation (D/H ratios) reveals a cold ($T_{\rm kin}\lesssim30$ K), relatively quiescent gas component embedded within the otherwise warm and turbulent CMZ, indicating that the earliest stages of star formation can survive in this extreme environment. I also present new $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C measurements from HC$_3$N and HC$_5$N, including the first constraints from doubly substituted $^{13}$C isotopologues. After accounting for isotopic fractionation with astrochemical models, the inferred elemental ratio ($\sim37$--48) exceeds the canonical CMZ assumed value ($\sim$20), supporting a scenario in which the Galactic center is replenished by less chemically processed gas flowing inward along the Galactic bar.

2610.11606.title: Radio Continuum Study of One of the Brightest Large Magellanic Cloud Supernova Remnants N 132D
2610.11606.abstract: We present a new radio continuum study of the Large Magellanic Cloud supernova remnant N 132D using observations from the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and MeerKAT. The radio morphology shows a clear spatial correlation with the X-ray emission in the central and left regions of the remnant, as well as in the right portion of the shell, indicating a close connection between the thermal and non-thermal plasma components. Polarisation measurements reveal predominantly radial magnetic fields, with mean fractional polarisations of 1.2 per cent, 3.0 per cent, and 4.0 per cent at 2100, 5500, and 9000 MHz, respectively. There is also a complex structure in the Faraday Depth spectrum, showing a double-peaked profile that indicates regions with differing magnetisation properties or varying magnetic field geometry. The rotation measure derived from ATCA data has an average value of ~2 rad m^-2, with a maximum of ~338 rad m^-2. We estimate a constant partition magnetic field of ~90 microG and a minimum energy of 3 x 10^50 erg, which is in a constant partition between the energy density of electrons and the energy density of the magnetic field. The integrated radio spectrum follows a power law with a spectral index of -0.74 +- 0.01. These results provide new constraints on the magnetic field structure and energetic properties of N 132D and offer insight into particle acceleration and shock evolution in young supernova remnants.

2610.13182.title: Flux Evolution of PSR B0540--69 and the Spectral Energy Distribution of its Pulsar Wind Nebula
2610.13182.abstract: The young Crab-like pulsar PSR B0540--69, located in the Large Magellanic Cloud, underwent a spin-down rate transition (SRT) in 2011 December, after which its pulsar wind nebula (PWN) was reported to brighten up to 2018. In this work, we extend the study of its X-ray and $γ$-ray flux evolution through 2026 by combining observations from multiple X-ray instruments with data from the Fermi Large Area Telescope, thereby constructing a flux history of the PSR$+$PWN system spanning more than two decades.
